The Prophet visited the unconscious Jabir and sprinkled his ablution water on him; Jabir woke and asked who would inherit from him, and the verses on inheritance were revealed.
Once offspring inherited and parents only by will, until Allah set shares: a male double a female, a sixth for each parent, and fixed shares for wife and husband.
The Prophet's heirs will not inherit a dinar or dirham, for what he leaves beyond his wives' support and his employees' wages is charity.
The Prophet's heirs take no Dinar, all beyond his wives' and workers' expenses being charity; he left some barley in Aisha's house, his arms, a white mule and charity land.
Asked to judge Ali and Abbas over Bani An-Nadir's fai, Umar cites the Prophet: prophets' property is not inherited but given in charity; Abu Bakr answers Fatima and Abbas likewise.
Abu Bakr refuses Fatima the Prophet's property, which the Prophet said is charity, not inheritance; after her death Ali, aggrieved at not being consulted, pledges allegiance to him.
The inheritance verses cover relatives present at the division, the shares of children, parents and spouses, the ban on inheriting women against their will, and ending inheritance by brotherhood.
Umar reminded Ali and Abbas, claiming the Prophet's estate, that what prophets leave is charity, not inheritance, and held them to manage it as the Prophet and Abu Bakr had.
The Prophet revived the ill Jabir with his ablution water, and when Jabir, with no son or father to inherit, asked about his estate, the verse of inheritance was revealed.
When Jabir lay unconscious the Prophet poured his ablution water over him; Jabir asked how to distribute his property, and the Prophet did not reply until the inheritance verses came.
The prophets' property is not inherited but spent in charity, after the family's provision, as Abu Bakr told Fatima and Al-Abbas, Umar told Ali and Abbas, and Aisha the wives.
The Prophet pays the debts of believers who die leaving nothing, while any property goes to the heirs: the prescribed shares first, then the remainder to the closest male relative.
A daughter takes half, a son's daughter a sixth, a sister the rest; shares come first, then the closest male; parents and spouses have fixed portions; Emigrant-Ansar brotherhood inheritance ended.
A sister's son belongs to her people; a man's property goes to his heirs, his debts and dependants to the Prophet; Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from each other.
When the sick Jabir, revived by the Prophet's ablution water, asked how to deal with his wealth, the Prophet gave no reply until the verse of inheritance was revealed.
